title: Memory Layout and Virtual Address Spaces in 2025
content:
Understanding Modern Memory Models

Modern operating systems use sophisticated virtual memory layouts that separate kernel and user spaces, enforce ASLR, and support memory-mapped I/O for performance.

Key Concepts

  • Page tables and hardware-assisted TLB lookups
  • Stack vs heap vs mmap regions
  • Shared memory across processes via shm_open()
  • Memory protection and segmentation faults

title: System Call Efficiency in the Post-vDSO Era
content:
Beyond Traditional syscalls

vDSO (virtual dynamic shared object) allows certain syscalls like gettimeofday() to execute entirely in userspace, bypassing kernel traps and improving latency-sensitive applications.

Performance Gains

  • Zero-kernel-path for time operations
  • Reduced context-switch overhead
  • Compiler-aware syscall inlining
  • Seccomp-BPF for secure syscall filtering

references.title: vDSO: Accelerating System Calls in Linux

title: eBPF: The New Kernel Extension Model
content:
Safe Kernel Programmability

eBPF enables developers to run sandboxed programs in the kernel without modifying kernel source or loading modules—ideal for observability, networking, and security.

Use Cases in 2025

  • Network packet filtering with XDP
  • Tracing kernel functions via kprobes
  • Custom schedulers and memory allocators
  • Real-time performance monitoring

Verified eBPF Programs via Static Analysis

title: io_uring: Asynchronous I/O Without the Overhead
content:
Revolutionizing I/O on Linux

io_uring provides a high-performance, scalable asynchronous I/O interface that avoids syscalls per operation by using shared kernel-user ring buffers.

Why It Matters

  • Millions of IOPS with minimal CPU usage
  • Zero-copy file and socket operations
  • Support for buffered and direct I/O
  • Native integration in SQLite and Redis

title: Rust in the Linux Kernel: Two Years On
content:
Safer Systems Development

Since Rust's official inclusion in the Linux kernel (v6.1), thousands of lines of driver code have been rewritten in Rust—reducing memory safety bugs by over 70%.

Key Advances

  • Ownership model prevents use-after-free
  • Zero-cost abstractions for embedded contexts
  • Seamless C interop via bindgen
  • Compiler-enforced concurrency safety

references.title: Rust for Linux: Annual Security Report

title: cgroups v2: Unified Resource Control for System Programmers
content:
Beyond Containers

cgroups v2 provides a unified hierarchy for CPU, memory, I/O, and network resource control—essential for building low-level schedulers and QoS engines.

System-Level Features

  • Pressure Stall Information (PSI) for congestion detection
  • Writeback throttling for SSD longevity
  • Thread mode for fine-grained control
  • BPF integration for dynamic policy enforcement

title: Next-Gen Memory Allocators: From dlmalloc to mimalloc
content:
Speed and Fragmentation Tradeoffs

Modern allocators like mimalloc, rpmalloc, and snmalloc prioritize low latency, NUMA awareness, and scalability across thousands of threads.

Design Principles

  • Per-thread arenas reduce lock contention
  • Lazy commit of virtual memory
  • Secure metadata to prevent heap exploits
  • Transparent huge page support

references.title: mimalloc: Free List Sharding in Practice

title: Unikernels in 2025: Specialized Systems Reborn
content:
Single-Address-Space Machines

Unikernels compile application and OS into a single binary, eliminating context switches and attack surfaces—ideal for edge computing and secure microservices.

Technical Highlights

  • Sub-millisecond boot times
  • No syscalls—direct hardware access via drivers
  • Compiled with OCaml, Rust, or C
  • Deployable on AWS Firecracker and QEMU

references.title: Unikernels: Library Operating Systems for the Cloud

title: Low-Latency Scheduling with PREEMPT_RT and Beyond
content:
Real-Time Systems on General-Purpose Kernels

The full upstreaming of PREEMPT_RT into Linux 6.12 enables hard real-time guarantees without custom kernels—critical for robotics and audio processing.

Key Mechanisms

  • Threaded interrupt handlers
  • Priority inheritance for mutexes
  • Reduced worst-case scheduling latency (< 50 µs)
  • Per-CPU runqueues with lockless design

title: Kernel Tracing with eBPF and BTF in 2025
content:
Observability Without Overhead

BTF (BPF Type Format) enables rich, type-safe tracing of kernel data structures without debug symbols—powering tools like bpftrace and Parca.

Capabilities

  • Profile CPU, memory, and lock contention
  • Dynamic function entry/exit probes
  • Stack walks with symbol resolution
  • Export metrics to OpenTelemetry

references.title: bpftrace: A Practical Guide to Linux Tracing
